artists.biography: The Avalanches are an Australian electronic music group formed in 1997 with mainstays Robbie Chater on keyboards, Tony Diblasi on keyboards, bass and backing vocals, and Darren Seltmann on vocals and keyboards. They are known for their live and recorded DJ sets and their debut album Since I Left You (2000), which they claim was assembled from approximately 3500 vinyl samples. The album peaked in the top 10 on the UK Albums Chart in April 2001. At the ARIA Music Awards of 2001, the group received nine nominations and won four categories: 'Best New Artist - Album' and 'Best Dance Release' for Since I Left You, 'Best New Artist - Single' for "Frontier Psychiatrist", and 'Producer of the Year' for Bobbydazzler (production name for Chater and Seltmann). In October 2010, the album was listed at No. 10 in the book, 100 Best Australian Albums. The Album has also been named # 1 Australian Album of all time in a Triple J industry poll, as well as # 10 album of the decade by Pitchfork Media. It is estimated in the decade since its release the album has gone on to sell well over 1,000,000 copies.

perplexity.description:
Wildflower is the second studio album by Australian electronic group The Avalanches, released in 2016 on XL Recordings and Modular Recordings. Following their acclaimed 2000 debut Since I Left You, the album arrived after a 16-year gap, marked by extensive production and sample clearance. Musically, Wildflower blends electronic, hip hop, and rock elements, continuing the group’s signature style of intricate sampling and genre fusion. The album features a kaleidoscopic sound palette, with lush textures, playful loops, and dynamic edits, often evoking a psychedelic, almost cinematic journey. Collaborations with a range of vocalists and musicians add further depth, while the album’s structure and sonic experimentation reflect both the group’s roots in plunderphonics and their evolution into more expansive sonic territory.

In the context of The Avalanches’ discography, Wildflower stands as a long-awaited follow-up that both honors and expands upon the legacy of their debut. It debuted at number one on the ARIA Albums Chart in Australia, marking the group’s first chart-topping album. Critics praised its ambitious production, inventive use of samples, and its ability to capture a sense of wonder and nostalgia, with many noting its successful balance of experimentalism and accessibility. The album was widely regarded as a triumphant return, reaffirming The Avalanches’ status as pioneers in electronic music.
